source.section: Form 540 lines 13 to 19 and 31 to 33 (PDF pages 39-40); PDF page 13 Line 18 standard deduction chart and Line 31; PDF page 75 Tax Rate Schedules; PDF page 39 Form 540 lines 7 and 9 ('X $153'); PDF page 12 Line 7 and Line 9; PDF page 14 Line 32 and the AGI Limitation Worksheet lines a to i; PDF page 39 Form 540 line 7 (box 2: enter 2) and line 9

worked: Married filing jointly, both 67: private pensions 250,000 and 170,000, interest 60,000 (not U.S. obligations), dividends 40,000; federal AGI = 250,000 + 170,000 + 60,000 + 40,000 = 520,000, which is 15,589 over the 504,411 joint limit (inside the phase-down range). Form 540 line 13 federal AGI = 520,000.00. Federal taxable income = 520,000.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction - 2 x 1,600.00 age-65 addition = 485,300.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtractions: none (private pensions need no adjustment on line 5, PDF page 60). Form 540 line 14 = 0.00. Additions (line 16): 0.00. Line 15 = line 17 California AGI = 520,000.00 - 0.00 = 520,000.00. Line 18 California standard deduction (married filing jointly, PDF page 13 chart) 11,412.00. Line 19 taxable income = 520,000.00 - 11,412.00 = 508,588.00. Tax on 508,588.00 by the projection's brackets: 22,158.00 x 1% = 221.58; 30,370.00 x 2% = 607.40; 30,376.00 x 4% = 1,215.04; 32,180.00 x 6% = 1,930.80; 30,364.00 x 8% = 2,429.12; 363,140.00 x 9.3% = 33,772.02; total 40,175.96. Line 31: Tax Rate Schedule Y (PDF page 75), from its printed base, gives 40,175.96. Line 11 exemptions: 2 personal x 153 and 2 senior x 153. Federal AGI 520,000.00 is more than 504,411.00: the projection removes the personal and senior credits, line 32 = 0.00. The form's AGI Limitation Worksheet (PDF page 14) would give: c = 15,589 over 504,411.00; d = 15,589 / 2,500 rounded up = 7; e = 7 x 6 = 42; f = 4 boxes on lines 7 and 9; g = 42 x 4 = 168; h = 612; i = 612 - 168 = 444 (zero or less enters 0); line 32 = 444. Line 33 = 40,175.96 - 0.00 = 40,175.96; no other credits (lines 34 to 47 nil), line 48 = 40,175.96. State income tax = 40,175.96. Expected follows the projection (credits removed at the limit); on the form the 4 credits would come to 444, not 0, so the form's tax would be 444.00 lower. This is the accepted phase-down approximation.
accepted_approximations: The exemption credits' AGI limitation is a stepped phase-down (each credit loses 6 for each 2,500 of federal AGI, or part of it, over 252,203 single and married filing separately, 504,411 joint and qualifying surviving spouse, 378,310 head of household; 1,250 steps when filing separately). The projection has no field for unprinted step amounts, so it removes the personal and senior credits at the threshold.
